title: ResMoE: Space-efficient Compression of Mixture of Experts LLMs via Residual Restoration

problem.claim: MoE Transformers activate only part of their parameters per token but still require all parameters to be loaded during inference, creating space inefficiency.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need for more space-efficient inference without retraining while preserving accuracy.

contributions.claim: ResMoE approximates MoE experts by extracting a shared Wasserstein-barycenter expert and modeling residuals relative to it.
The framework enables one-shot, data-agnostic compression of large-scale MoE Transformers without retraining.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on Switch Transformer, Mixtral, and DeepSeekMoE models.
The authors report reducing parameters in an expert by up to 75% while maintaining comparable performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: MoE Transformers use sparse activation across model parameters.
Inference remains space-inefficient because all parameters must be loaded.
ResMoE represents experts through a shared barycenter expert and residual approximations.
The approach targets one-shot, data-agnostic inference compression without retraining and with limited accuracy loss.
Experiments across three MoE model families are reported, including expert parameter reduction of up to 75%.

source_observation.claim: A shared expert representation is paired with residuals to approximate multiple experts.

interpretation.claim: Common structure can be factored out before storing model-specific differences.

application.claim: For collections of related modules, evaluate shared-basis or prototype-plus-residual compression.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when residual approximation will preserve performance across other architectures or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the accuracy metrics, baselines, datasets, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not quantify inference memory savings or the computational cost of compression.
The abstract does not describe the approximation algorithm or its error guarantees.
